study.title: 1 Chronicles 28 David delivers the temple design and responsibility to Solomon
study.overview: This chapter shows David at the end of his life by gathering the leaders of Israel to transfer Solomon not only the government, but also the task of building the house of the LORD. The center of David's speech is not only the material work: it is the sovereignty of God, who chooses specific people, requires obedience and gives direction to worship. The chapter ends with practical encouragement: Solomon will not be alone, for there will be priests, Levites, volunteer craftsmen, princes and all the people to help him. Thus, the text unites vocation, holiness, planning and community cooperation.

outline.title: David gathers Israel and declares Solomon's choice
outline.explanation: David summons the chiefs of Israel and explains that he wanted to build a house for the ark, but God did not allow him to build it for being a man of war. He then states that the LORD chose him and also chose Solomon to occupy the throne and build the house, linking the monarchy to the divine promise and obedience to the covenant.

outline.title: Public exhortation to obedience and faithful service
outline.explanation: David speaks before all Israel, and exhorts the people to keep the commandments of the LORD to remain in the good land. Then he addresses Solomon with a personal call: to know God, to serve him wholeheartedly and to seek him with seriousness, because God knows the inner intentions and answers both to the sincere pursuit and to abandonment.

outline.title: The temple model, resources and final encouragement
outline.explanation: David gives Solomon the detailed drawing of the temple and the utensils, attributing to God the origin of this plan. He also distributes gold and silver by weight to the various objects and recalls the organization of worship with priests and Levites. Finally, it encourages Solomon not to fear, assuring that God will be with him and that many collaborators will be available for the execution of the work.

study.context: The chapter belongs to the closure of David's narrative and presents a solemn meeting of Israel's leaders in Jerusalem. The notes provided highlight that this discourse continues the transition from David's authority to Solomon and that the central theme is the construction of the temple. It is also noteworthy, based on the notes, that the "repous" of the ark indicates stability after the time of war, and that David received by divine inspiration the model of the house of the LORD.
study.theology: The text teaches that God governs history by choosing people and assigning specific functions to them. David does not correct God's purpose; he submits to him. The construction of the temple is not presented as a human project of prestige, but as a work sanctified by the divine initiative, by caring for worship and obedience to the covenant. There is also a strong emphasis on personal responsibility: Solomon must know God, serve him with sincerity and persevere; the people must keep the commandments; and the permanence of blessing is linked to faithfulness. At the same time, the chapter shows that God uses concrete means - planning, materials, servers and leadership - to accomplish his purposes.

scholarViews.insight: The temple is described as a place of rest of the ark, indicating peace and stability after the period of conquest; with this, the presence of the covenant begins to remain in Jerusalem.
David closes his life well by calling on the leaders, handing Solomon the honor of building the temple and treating piety as the central duty of king and people.
David presents to Solomon the assistants of the work - priests, Levites, volunteer artisans, princes and people - to show that the task would be carried out with broad cooperation.

questions: What does the text teach about the relationship between human planning and God's direction in the temple work?
How does the exhortation to Solomon in 1 Chronicles 28:9 confronts an external religiosity only?
How can the promise of help in 1 Chronicles 28:21 encourage church projects today without turning cooperation into self-confidence?
study.practice: Submit your plans to God before executing them, as David did; when there is a responsibility given by God, take it with courage, obedience, and whole heart. In practice, this means seeking the will of the Lord sincerely, to organize resources responsibly and to count on the collaboration of the people of God without losing sight of the view that the work belongs to the Lord. It is also a call for leaders and communities not to separate worship, character and service.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided do not allow to safely state additional historical details beyond what the chapter itself and the commentators mention. The descriptions of the exact origin of the temple model, the form of his communication to David and some biblical parallels are interpretations of the commentators, not given explicit by the text of 1 Chronicles 28. There is no basis for notes to deepen dates, specific geography or archaeological reconstructions.
